mira: FYI ran a nightly perf sweep on the batcher; saw OOM kills on node-7 during long-chat mix (avg seq_len 512, kv entries ~120MB).
jon: Can you paste the p95 latency and mem graphs?
mira: p95 CPU <-> GPU time looks fine. Memory climbs when batch token sum > 12k and kv cache is heavily used. p95 latency spikes +200ms right before OOM.
sam: So batch formation is not accounting for per-request KV footprint. We should gate admission with estimated_kv_size + token_budget.
lee: We already have min_headroom_bytes=256MB global. Could be too small for these tails.
alex: Idea: compute per-req kv_est = num_kv_entries * avg_entry_size(req.model) and keep a rolling 95th percentile. Require free_kv_mem >= kv_est*1.2 + token_budget_est*per_token_kv_overhead.
mira: I prototyped a simple admission check that does that. Admission condition: free_kv_mem - kv_est >= reserve_floor. reserve_floor is dynamic = max(global_min, pct_of_total_kv_mem). Canaryed it on 3 nodes.

mira: ```
# pseudocode
kv_est = req.kv_entries * avg_entry_size(req.model)
if free_kv_mem - kv_est < reserve_floor:
    reject_or_delay(req)
else:
    admit(req)
```

perf-bot: nightly-run: canary reduced OOMs from 5 -> 0 across 48h, p99 latency increased ~30ms at peak.
jon: Nice. What's the impact on throughput (qps)?
mira: Throughput down ~3% for kv-heavy mixes, but tail stability is much better.
sam: We need a queue policy for delayed requests: prefer admitting small-token requests first, or split/stream very large requests. Also consider steering to a kernel variant that supports on-the-fly KV eviction.
lee: Kernel selection matters: kv-friendly kernels with streaming eviction avoid OOM but add ~8% per-token latency. Might be ok if it prevents OOM.
alex: We can also set a dynamic token_budget target: target = base_target * (1 - kv_pressure_factor). kv_pressure_factor derived from moving avg of delayed_kv_bytes/total_kv_mem.
mira: Proposal: ship an adaptive_flooring module that 1) estimates per-req kv, 2) computes reserve_floor per GPU, 3) gates admission and exposes telemetry counters for reason codes.
sam: Add experiment flags: adaptive_floor_v1 and kv_estimator_v2. Can we run infra canary tomorrow night?
mira: I'll schedule a canary with those flags; deploy window 10pm PST. TL;DR: per-req KV estimator + dynamic reserve floor cuts OOMs, small throughput hit, need broader perf/regression checks.
jon: :thumbsup: Please add unit tests for estimator with synthetic KV entries and a fuzz test for corner cases.
alex: Also add metrics: admitted_kv_bytes, delayed_kv_bytes, reserve_floor_bytes per node. That will help correlate.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for 2361190000 to eng-runtime-canary.
lee: I'll review the kernel routing patch; if ok we merge to staging.
mira: Thanks — will post canary results + perf dashboards in this thread after 48h.
